issues.quote: `if (mounted)` guards this last `setState`: the user may have left the screen while the request was running, and `finally` runs anyway
issues.text: The reason is now clear, but it fits the two `setState` calls in `try` and `catch` too: they also run after the request ends, when the user may have left. The code guards only the last one, and I cannot tell from the text whether the other two are fine or just unguarded.
issues.fix: Add half a sentence saying what happens to the two earlier `setState` calls if the user has left, or say plainly that only the last one is guarded in this stage.

issues.quote: `finally` enables the button again, so a later tap places a second, separate order on purpose; `if (mounted)` guards this last `setState`: the user may have left the screen
issues.text: One sentence carries two ideas (the button coming back, and the `mounted` guard) joined by a semicolon and then a colon. I had to read it twice to see where the second idea starts.
issues.fix: Split at the semicolon: end the first sentence after "on purpose." and start a new sentence with "`if (mounted)` guards this last `setState`."
